title: High-post flash
summary: Play through #99 in the middle, with #19 behind the zone.
notes:
First read: #99 scores if the centre stays low. If the centre comes up, find #19 behind him. Keep #6 available for the reversal and #11 wide.

AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Use #99’s middle catch to make the centre choose between #99 and #19. Flash into an open gap; do not force a covered entry.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#99 cuts to get free from his own defender. If denied, use #19’s screen or a backdoor cut; the foul line is not automatically open against man.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

frames.label: 1. Entry
frames.note: 6 → 11; #99 flashes to the foul line. #19 stays behind the centre.

frames.label: 2. Feed #99
frames.note: 11 → 99; face the rim. If the centre stays low, #99 shoots or drives.

frames.label: 3. Find #19
frames.note: Centre steps up: 99 → 19, then #19 finishes. #64 seals the weak side.

frames.label: #6 kick-out
frames.note: Top defenders pinch in: 99 → 6 for the open shot or closeout attack.

title: Overload + inside seal
summary: Load one side, then reverse to an inside flash.
notes:
Use the overload to create a decision for the low defender. Reverse the ball if that side stays covered. #64 screens the centre as #19 flashes.

AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Reverse when the overloaded side stays covered. #64 delays the centre and #19 flashes into the newly opened middle.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
Loading one side does not create the same numerical advantage against man. Use #64 to screen #19’s defender, and have #99 attack a closeout if the post catch is denied.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

frames.label: 1. Entry + fill
frames.note: 6 → 99, then #6 cuts to the corner; #11 fills the top. #64 starts high.

frames.label: 2. Reverse + seal
frames.note: 99 → 11; #64 seals the centre as #19 flashes into the lane.

frames.label: 3. Feed #19
frames.note: 11 → 19 before the zone recovers. #99 and #6 keep the right side wide.

frames.label: #6 corner read
frames.note: If the low defender stays inside: 99 → 6 in the corner.

title: Zone ball screen
summary: Let #99 attack a top defender’s screen, with #19 rolling.
notes:
Set a stationary screen with space for the defender. #99 attacks with his head up. #19 rolls only after the screen; #11 holds the corner.

AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Screen a top defender to create a gap. Read the centre on the drive and the low defender on the corner pass.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#19 screens #99’s defender and rolls. #99 reads under, trail or switch, and passes only after help commits.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

frames.label: 1. Entry + screen
frames.note: 6 → 99; #19 screens the right top defender. #11 holds the corner.

frames.label: 2. #99 attacks
frames.note: #99 turns the corner; #19 rolls. If the lane stays open, #99 finishes.

frames.label: 3. #19 rolls
frames.note: Centre stops #99: 99 → 19 rolling inside. #64 stays out of the lane.

frames.label: #11 corner read
frames.note: Low-right defender helps: 99 → 11 in the corner. #6 is the top outlet.

title: Runner
summary: Free #99 with a baseline run and #19’s screen.
notes:
Time the baseline run with the pass. #19 screens the low defender; after screening he seals inside. If #99 is open, take the shot.

AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Run behind the low line as the ball arrives on the entry side. Shoot the free corner catch or find the inside seal.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#19 screens #99’s own defender. #99 runs shoulder-to-shoulder off the screen; curl a trailing defender or fade if the defender goes underneath.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

frames.label: 1. Entry
frames.note: 6 → 11. #99 starts in the opposite corner; #19 prepares the baseline screen.

frames.label: 2. Baseline run
frames.note: #99 runs behind the zone, using #19’s screen to reach the right corner.

frames.label: 3. Find #99
frames.note: 11 → 99 for the corner shot. #19 seals inside; #64 flashes as an outlet.

frames.label: Inside counter
frames.note: If the closeout takes #99’s shot away, feed #19’s seal. #64 is the middle outlet.

title: Runner Pin
summary: Counter Runner with a change of direction and a skip.
notes:
Sell the initial run. #99 changes direction behind #64’s pin screen. The skip pass must be clearly open; use a pass fake if the defender reads it.

AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Make the fake baseline run believable. Skip back only when the passing lane is open; #64 pins the low defender on the return side.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#64 pins #99’s defender on the return route. If the defender top-locks the corner, look for an open backdoor route instead of forcing the skip.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

frames.label: 1. Entry
frames.note: 6 → 11. Start like Runner, with #99 in the left corner.

frames.label: 2. Fake run
frames.note: #99 starts across the baseline, then turns back. #64 prepares the pin screen.

frames.label: 3. Skip back
frames.note: #99 returns to the left corner behind #64’s screen; #11 skips the ball across.

frames.label: Catch + read
frames.note: #99 takes the open shot. #64 seals inside; #19 offers a middle outlet if covered.

title: Short-corner dive
summary: Get #19 the ball beside the paint, then send #99 behind the centre.
notes:
Make the short-corner pass before starting the dive. #99 goes behind the centre; #11 clears toward the corner. #19 reads the inside pass or kick-out.

AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
The short-corner catch pulls attention down and outside. #99 dives only as #19 receives, then reads the centre and the kick-out.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#19 first establishes position on his own defender. #99 cuts behind a helping defender, or uses #64’s screen if his defender stays attached.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

frames.label: 1. Entry
frames.note: 6 → 11. #19 slides to the short corner; #99 flashes into the middle.

frames.label: 2. Short corner
frames.note: 11 → 19. On that catch, #99 dives to the right block and #11 slides to the corner.

frames.label: 3. #99 dives
frames.note: If the centre moves toward #19, hit #99 underneath. #64 stays on the weak side.

frames.label: #11 kick-out
frames.note: If the low defender protects #99’s dive, #19 passes back out to #11 in the corner.

notes: These are proposed 2–3 assignments based on the roles described, not a reconstruction of a game possession. Mirror on the other side. Keep #19 central only if he is your strongest interior defender. Move on the pass and communicate before handing off the ball.

title: DHO: #6 hands to #99
summary: A simple perimeter handoff that gets #99 moving into a gap.

frames.label: 1. Bring the handoff
frames.note: #6 dribbles toward the left slot; #99 lifts from the wing to meet him.

frames.label: 2. Handoff
frames.note: #6 gives the ball to #99 and becomes a stationary screen. Meet close; the player spacing here is schematic.

frames.label: 3. Read the front guard
frames.note: #99 shoots if the zone stays low. If the guard steps up, attack the left gap; #6 replaces to the top.

frames.label: 4. Help commits
frames.note: If the centre stops #99, find #19 behind him through an open passing lane. #11 holds the opposite wing.

notes:
AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Use this when a top zone defender is willing to come out. #99 receives above the zone, then shoots if the defender stays back or attacks the gap if he closes. The handoff alone does not remove the low defenders; read the centre before continuing.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#99 comes tight off #6. If his defender trails, turn the corner; if the defender goes under and the shot is in range, shoot. On a switch, face up and read the matchup.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

TIMING / SPACING
Make the transfer shoulder-to-shoulder. #6 stops before screening and keeps arms in. #19 stays behind the centre; #64 holds the short corner to keep the driving path open.

title: Zoom / Chicago: screen into handoff
summary: Free #99 from the corner with #64’s screen, then #11’s handoff.

frames.label: 1. Entry
frames.note: #6 passes to #11 at the right slot, then clears to the left slot.

frames.label: 2. Screen + lift
frames.note: #64 screens the low-right zone defender. #99 lifts from the corner as #11 brings the ball toward him.

frames.label: 3. Handoff
frames.note: #11 hands to #99. #64 clears inside after the screen; #19 holds the weak side.

frames.label: 4. Turn the corner
frames.note: #99 reads the top guard: take the open shot or attack the gap. #11 clears to the right corner.

frames.label: 5. Corner read
frames.note: If the low-right defender helps on #99, kick to #11 in the corner. #19 seals on the weak side.

notes:
AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
The first screen delays the low defender; the handoff changes the angle of attack. #99 reads the next top defender, then the low defender. If the zone passes him off cleanly, use the open outside shot, corner pass or reversal instead of driving into three defenders.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
#64 screens #99’s own defender. #99 sets the defender up, comes tight off the screen and receives from #11 at speed. Overplay can create a backdoor cut if the lane is clear.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

TIMING / SPACING
#64 sets before #99 arrives. #11 delivers the handoff as #99 exits the screen, then clears the corner. Keep #19 on the weak side until help commits.

title: Fake handoff: #99 keeps
summary: Use #6’s handoff threat to open an inside driving lane for #99.

frames.label: 1. Entry
frames.note: #6 enters to #99 at the right slot; #11 spaces left and #19 stays inside on the weak side.

frames.label: 2. Show the handoff
frames.note: #6 runs toward #99 as if taking the ball. #99 keeps it only if the top defender commits toward #6.

frames.label: 3. Keep + attack
frames.note: #99 keeps and attacks the inside gap. #6 continues to the right corner, clearing the lane.

frames.label: 4. Read the centre
frames.note: If the centre steps up, #99 can feed #19 underneath. If the low-right defender helps, #6 is the corner outlet.

notes:
AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
Call this as a counter after a real handoff has made the top defender react. If the defender stays in position, make the real handoff or reverse the ball. On the keep, #99 still has to read the centre rather than force a layup.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
Keep the ball when the defender cheats to stop #6 receiving. #6 continues his cut to clear space; #99 attacks the opening and passes if help stops him.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

TIMING / SPACING
Show the same entry as the real handoff. Do not push or hook a defender. #6 must keep moving after the fake; both handlers standing together would kill the spacing.

title: Block Baseline: #99 cuts underneath
summary: Lift the low defender, seal the centre and send #99 behind the zone.

frames.label: 1. Freeze the top guard
frames.note: #6 dribbles toward the right top defender to hold him. #11 waits below the free-throw-line extended.

frames.label: 2. Wing entry
frames.note: #6 passes to #11. Run the baseline action only if the low-right defender comes out to the ball; #19 sets the centre screen.

frames.label: 3. Baseline cut
frames.note: #99 cuts below the centre from the left block to the right side. #19 holds his legal position to delay the centre’s rotation.

frames.label: 4. Inside catch
frames.note: #11 finds #99 behind the lifted low defender. #99 stops in the passing window rather than running through it.

notes:
AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
This is a documented 2–3-zone set. Its trigger is the low defender coming out to #11. #19 screens the centre and #99 crosses underneath into the open block. If the top guard covers #11 and the low defender stays home, reverse the ball; the intended inside window has not opened.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
Adapt #19’s screen to #99’s own defender. #99 comes tight off the cross-screen and seals after a switch. Do not assume the middle defender is the correct screening target against man.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

TIMING / SPACING
Wing entry first, centre screen second, cutter third. Keep the screen stationary and give a defender who cannot see it room to react. #99 shows hands and stops for the catch.

title: Anchors X-cut: middle flash + dive
summary: On reversal, #99 dives first and #19 flashes through the middle second.

frames.label: 1. Entry right
frames.note: #6 passes to #11. #99 starts high on the right; #19 starts low on that side.

frames.label: 2. Reverse
frames.note: #11 returns the ball to #6 to move the zone back across.

frames.label: 3. Dive first
frames.note: #6 moves to the left wing; #64 fills the top around the outside. #99 cuts from the high post down to the left block FIRST.

frames.label: 4. Middle cut second
frames.note: After #99 clears the crossing point, #19 flashes diagonally from the right short corner into the left middle gap.

frames.label: 5. High-low read
frames.note: #6 finds #19 in the middle. If the centre comes up, #19 gives the quick high-low pass to #99 below him.

notes:
AGAINST A 2–3 ZONE
This adapts the Anchors post X-cut used against a 2–3. Reverse the ball, then send the HIGH player first and the LOW player second. The crossing cuts force the zone to cover two different levels. #19 faces the rim and reads #99 underneath; he can finish himself if the middle is open.

AGAINST HALF-COURT MAN
Use the post exchange to cut across your own defenders and establish inside position. If both catches are denied, flow into #19 screening for #6 while #99 clears or seals, rather than forcing a pass through a covered zone-style gap.

AGAINST FULL-COURT MAN
Beat pressure first. #6, #11 or #99 can advance the ball; offer a return pass. Take an open breakaway, otherwise organise this set in the frontcourt.

TIMING / SPACING
Stagger the cuts. #99 goes first, #19 follows after the paths clear. #64 stays as the reversal outlet; #11 keeps the far wing available. Neither cutter waits in the lane.
